criterion_checks.rationale: The teacher describes six distinct inattentive symptoms in science class.

criterion_checks.requirement: Relevant symptoms have persisted for at least six months.
criterion_checks.rationale: The reported classroom difficulties have lasted about nine months.

assessment_rationale: The source supports six inattentive symptoms, a duration of about nine months, and academic impairment. However, the reported onset is after age 12 and concerns are limited to science class, so two specified constraints are not met. This assessment does not assert a diagnosis.
source_case_material: A 13-year-old student has had difficulty staying focused in science class for about nine months. The science teacher reports that the student overlooks details in lab instructions, loses focus during independent work, appears not to hear questions, leaves written tasks unfinished, struggles to keep class materials organized, and often misplaces handouts. The student’s science grade has declined, and assignments are frequently incomplete. The caregiver reports no similar concerns during homework or other activities at home. The family and school agree that these classroom difficulties first became noticeable around age 12 years and 6 months; they report no earlier pattern.

functional_impairment.evidence: The science grade has declined, and assignments are frequently incomplete.

target_constraint_specification: Assess only these prespecified constraints: for a child under 17, at least six distinct inattentive symptoms are supported; relevant symptoms have persisted for at least six months; onset is supported before age 12; symptoms are reported in at least two settings; and symptoms are associated with functional impairment. Do not make a diagnosis beyond these constraints.
